newsitem.title: JAPAN: Support for Japan's Hashimoto drops to 36.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Support for Japan's Hashimoto drops to 36.1 pct.

text.p: The support rate for Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's cabinet has slumped to 36.1 percent, the lowest level since he took office a year ago, an opinion poll showed on Tuesday.
The poll by the Nihon Keizai Shimbun business daily, conducted last weekend, showed an 11 percentage point drop in support from a similar poll in January.
Those surveyed cited "Hashimoto's lack of leadership" and "bad policies" as reasons for their lack of support, the newspaper said.
Hashimoto's first cabinet in January 1996 was a coalition grouping his conservative Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), the Socialists and the Sakigake Party, an LDP splinter group.
The LDP returned to sole power in Lower House elections last October.
The latest cabinet support rating is the lowest in a Nihon Keizai Shimbun poll of Hashimoto's term of office so far.
The survey covered 3,000 people, of whom 59 percent responded. The newspaper did not say what its previous record low for Hashimoto's cabinet was.
